(An Appeal U/S.173 Of M.V. Act vs Banamali Das & Others on 7
November, 2025

Author: G. Satapathy
Bench: G. Satapathy
 In The High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
 Maca No.569 of 2022
 (An appeal U/S.173 of M.V. Act, 1988).
 Mandakini Muduli ... Appellant
 -versus-
 Banamali Das & others ...

entities.text: High Court Of Orissa At Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Respondents
 For Appellant : Mr. B.B. Singh, Adv.
 For Respondents : Mr. P.K. Mishra, Adv.
 (R-3 & 4)
 Mr. S.K. Sahoo, Adv.
 (R-2)
 Coram:
 Justice G. Satapathy
 Date Of Hearing & Date Of Judgment

:07.11.2025(ORAL)
G. Satapathy, J.
1.

This is an appeal U/S. 173 of the MV Act by the claimant-widow of the deceased seeking enhancement of compensation as well as challenging the apportionment of the award to Respondents- Claimant Nos.3 and 4(R3&4).

By the impugned common judgment dated 13.09.2022 passed in MAC No. 584 of 2017 and MAC No. 589 of 2017, the 3rd Addl. District Judge-cum-5th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Balasore (In short "the learned tribunal") has not only allowed the two separate claim applications filed one by the parents and another by widow of the deceased against the Respondent No.2(R2)-Insurer on contest and exparte against the owner of the offending vehicle, but also has directed the R2-cum-Insurer to pay compensation of Rs. 11,05,200/- along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on Rs. 7,98,000/-excluding Rs.3,07,200/- which was awarded towards future prospects w.e.f 27.12.2017 till realization, besides Rs.40,000/- to the parents-claimants towards filial consortium.
2. In the course of hearing, Mr. Bishnu Brata Singh, learned counsel for the appellant not pressed the claim of the appellant for enhancement, but he contends that the matter has been amicably settled between the parties in the mediation proceeding with regard to apportionment of the amount (An Appeal U/S.173 Of M.V. Act vs Banamali Das & Others on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143740679/
1 and such mediation report is available on record.

entities.text: 3rd Addl. District Judge-cum-5th Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Balasore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In reply, Mr. Pradeep Kumar Mishra, learned counsel for the R3&4- cum-claimants parents does not dispute about settlement of the matter in the mediation proceeding.

Mr. S.K. Sahoo, learned counsel for the R2-cum- insurer has made it very clear that the insurer has already deposited the amount with the tribunal and he has got no say about the apportionment and prays to pass appropriate order for apportionment of the amount.
None appears for Respondent-owner who was in fact set exparte by the learned tribunal in the trial and he has not been saddled with any liability.
Further, Mr. Singh and Mr. Mishra, however, jointly prays to pass order in terms of the terms and conditions of the settlement arrived at between the parties at the mediation proceeding.

3. After having considered the rival submissions upon perusal of record, there is no dispute with regard to the appellant filing separate claim by impleading the insurer and owner of the offending vehicle as well as the parents filing another claim by impleading the owner and insurer of the offending vehicle.

Looking at the dispute between the parties, this Court in a special drive for mediation has referred both the parties to High Court of Orissa, Mediation Centre, Aain Seva Bhawan, Cuttack by an order passed on 28.07.2025 and accordingly, the mediator has submitted the mediation report by enclosing the terms and conditions of settlement between the parties which are extracted hereunder:-
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE COMPROMISE

entities.text: High Court of Orissa, Mediation Centre, Aain Seva Bhawan, Cuttack
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 1. The appellant Smt. Mandakini Muduli shall be entitled to 30% of the total compensation amount, as against the earlier share of 15% fixed by the Tribunal.
2. The Respondent Nos. 3 & 4 each shall be entitled to 35% of the compensation amount.
3. It is recorded that the Respondent No.2 (M/s. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.) has already deposited the awarded amount before the learned Tribunal.

entities.text: ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.
entities.label: RESPONDENT

sentences.text: 4. Both parties have agreed that the settlement fully and finally resolves the dispute regarding apportionment of compensation amount.
5. The parties have entered into this compromise of their own free will without any coercion or due influence or misinterpretation.

4. In view of the above facts and taking into consideration the undisputed settlement arrived at by the parties with regard to apportionment of the award and the appellant having forgone her claim for enhancement, this appeal is accordingly, allowed in terms of the settlement arrived at by the parties in the mediation proceeding and the terms and conditions of settlement shall form part of the judgment/award.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment is modified and the learned tribunal is hereby directed to disburse the amount in terms of the settlement arrived at by the parties in the mediation proceeding.

The insurance company is accordingly, directed to take back the invalid cheques which it had deposited before the learned tribunal and deposit fresh valid cheques towards (An Appeal U/S.173 Of M.V. Act vs Banamali Das & Others on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143740679/
2 payment of compensation to the parties in terms of the mediation report as referred to above.

opennyai_summary.facts: This is an appeal U/S. 173 of the MV Act by the claimant-widow of the deceased seeking enhancement of compensation as well as challenging the apportionment of the award to Respondents- Claimant Nos.3 and 4(R3&4).
opennyai_summary.arguments:
None appears for Respondent-owner who was in fact set exparte by the learned tribunal in the trial and he has not been saddled with any liability.
Further, Mr. Singh and Mr. Mishra, however, jointly prays to pass order in terms of the terms and conditions of the settlement arrived at between the parties at the mediation proceeding.

opennyai_summary.decision:
Looking at the dispute between the parties, this Court in a special drive for mediation has referred both the parties to High Court of Orissa, Mediation Centre, Aain Seva Bhawan, Cuttack by an order passed on 28.07.2025 and accordingly, the mediator has submitted the mediation report by enclosing the terms and conditions of settlement between the parties which are extracted hereunder:-
TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE COMPROMISE
1. The appellant Smt. Mandakini Muduli shall be entitled to 30% of the total compensation amount, as against the earlier share of 15% fixed by the Tribunal.
2. The Respondent Nos. 3 & 4 each shall be entitled to 35% of the compensation amount.
3. It is recorded that the Respondent No.2 (M/s. ICICI Lombard General Insurance Co. Ltd.) has already deposited the awarded amount before the learned Tribunal.
4. Both parties have agreed that the settlement fully and finally resolves the dispute regarding apportionment of compensation amount.
5. The parties have entered into this compromise of their own free will without any coercion or due influence or misinterpretation.
4. In view of the above facts and taking into consideration the undisputed settlement arrived at by the parties with regard to apportionment of the award and the appellant having forgone her claim for enhancement, this appeal is accordingly, allowed in terms of the settlement arrived at by the parties in the mediation proceeding and the terms and conditions of settlement shall form part of the judgment/award.
Accordingly, the impugned judgment is modified and the learned tribunal is hereby directed to disburse the amount in terms of the settlement arrived at by the parties in the mediation proceeding.
The insurance company is accordingly, directed to take back the invalid cheques which it had deposited before the learned tribunal and deposit fresh valid cheques towards (An Appeal U/S.173 Of M.V. Act vs Banamali Das & Others on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/143740679/
2 payment of compensation to the parties in terms of the mediation report as referred to above.
Needless to say that for the purpose of disbursing the compensation amount to the parties, the filial consortium as granted to the parents shall also include in the total compensation amount.
